raw_segments.text: Let us then take in the whole compass of this doctrine, and allow that the sentiment of
belief is nothing but a conception more intense and steady than what attends the mere fictions
of the imagination, and that this manner of conception arises from a customary conjunction
of the object with something present to the memory or senses.
I believe that it will not be difficult, upon these suppositions, to find other operations
of the mind analogous to it, and to trace up these phenomena to principles still more general.
